fatal_errors: The proposed material is martensitic steel rather than the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
It incorrectly excludes compositionally complex and high-entropy alloys, directly contradicting the target finding.
The proposed grain-boundary impurity-segregation mechanism is the conventional baseline mechanism, not the L12-ordering and jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary mechanism.
It omits the critical aging conditions near 600°C for maximum embrittlement and 750°C for ductility recovery.
No supporting evidence is provided for the claimed steel-based ductile-brittle-ductile sequence.
explanation: The hypothesis captures only the generic idea of a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response under heat treatment. It misses the central scientific result: as-cast FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 develops minimum ductility after aging near 600°C because enhanced L12 ordering raises APBE and promotes planar slip while jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips concentrate stress; ductility then recovers near 750°C as ordering decreases and ductile transition zones form. The proposed steel mechanism instead restates classical temper embrittlement, which serves as the comparison case in the target. Its experiment could test impurity segregation in steel but would not reconstruct or directly test the target phase-boundary and ordering mechanism.
